stem: Measurement is the process of comparing an unknown quantity with a __________.
solution: Measurement compares an unknown quantity with an agreed standard called a unit.

stem: The SI unit of length is the __________.
solution: The metre (m) is the SI unit of length.

stem: 1 metre is equal to __________ centimetres.
solution: 1 metre = 100 centimetres.

stem: 1 kilometre is equal to __________ metres.
solution: 1 kilometre = 1000 metres.

stem: 1 centimetre equals __________ millimetres.
solution: 1 centimetre = 10 millimetres.

stem: Why were early body-based units like the cubit and handspan replaced by standard units?
options: They varied from person to person and gave inconsistent results
They were too large to use
solution: Body-based measures differ between people, so standard units were adopted for consistent, comparable measurement.

stem: To measure the length of a curved line, the most suitable tool is a __________.
solution: A flexible thread can be laid along the curve and then measured against a straight scale.

stem: While measuring length with a scale, the eye should be kept __________ the reading to avoid error.
solution: The eye must be directly in line with the mark to avoid a parallax error in the reading.

stem: The error caused by looking at a scale reading from the wrong angle is called __________.
solution: Viewing a scale from an angle instead of straight on causes a parallax error.

stem: If the end of a ruler is broken, you should measure length by __________.
options: starting from a clear mark (e.g., the 1 cm mark) and subtracting
solution: Start from a full, clear mark and subtract its value from the final reading to avoid using the damaged end.

stem: An object is said to be in motion if its __________ changes with time relative to its surroundings.
solution: Motion is a change in an object's position with time relative to a reference point.

stem: An object whose position does not change with time relative to its surroundings is said to be at __________.
solution: An object at rest keeps the same position relative to its surroundings over time.

stem: The motion of a ball moving along a straight road is an example of __________ motion.
solution: Motion along a straight line is called rectilinear motion.

stem: The motion of the hands of a clock or a fan blade is __________ motion.
solution: The tip of a clock hand or fan blade moves in a circle — circular (rotational) motion.

stem: The to-and-fro motion of a swing or a pendulum is called __________ motion.
solution: A swing or pendulum repeats a to-and-fro path — oscillatory (periodic) motion.

stem: The motion of a moving car's wheel is a combination of __________.
solution: A rolling wheel spins (rotational) while its axle moves forward (rectilinear) — a combination of both.

stem: Which of the following is an example of periodic motion?
options: A stone falling once from a height
A car moving on a straight road once
A ball rolling to a stop
solution: Periodic motion repeats at regular intervals, like a pendulum's swing.

stem: A measuring tape marked in centimetres and metres is most suitable for measuring __________.
options: the length of a room or cloth
very tiny objects under a microscope
solution: A measuring tape is convenient for longer, everyday lengths such as rooms and cloth.

stem: Which unit is most suitable to express the distance between two cities?
solution: Large distances like those between cities are conveniently expressed in kilometres.

stem: Which unit is most suitable for the thickness of a coin?
solution: The small thickness of a coin is best measured in millimetres.

stem: The distance covered by an object in a given time tells us about its __________.
solution: Speed relates the distance moved to the time taken — how fast an object moves.

stem: Which of the following statements about motion is correct?
options: Whether an object is in motion depends on the reference point chosen
Motion is the same for all observers regardless of reference
An object at rest can never appear to move
solution: Motion is relative: it depends on the chosen reference point; a passenger is at rest relative to the train but in motion relative to the ground.

stem: 0.5 metre is equal to __________ centimetres.
250 centimetres equals __________ metres.
To measure the girth (distance around) a tree trunk, the best tool is a __________.
solution: A flexible tape or thread can wrap around the curved trunk to measure its girth.

stem: Standard units are important mainly because they __________.
options: allow everyone everywhere to understand and compare measurements
solution: Standard units give the same value everywhere, enabling universal understanding and comparison.

stem: A person walks around a circular track and returns to the starting point. The type of motion is __________.
solution: Moving along a circular track is circular motion, even if the person returns to the start.

stem: Which of the following pairs a quantity with its correct SI unit?
solution: The SI unit of length is the metre; kilogram is mass, litre is volume, second is time.

stem: The plucked string of a musical instrument shows __________ motion.
solution: A vibrating string moves back and forth rapidly — vibratory (oscillatory) motion.

stem: While measuring, taking the reading at the point where the object ends against the scale requires that the __________.
options: scale is placed along the object with a clear starting mark
scale is held far from the object
solution: For an accurate reading, the scale must lie along the object with a defined starting mark and the eye kept in line.

stem: The motion of the Earth around the Sun is best described as __________.
options: periodic (repeating each year) and roughly circular
solution: The Earth's revolution around the Sun repeats every year (periodic) along a near-circular (elliptical) path.

stem: A metre scale is usually divided into the smallest markings of __________.
solution: A standard metre scale has centimetre markings each divided into 10 millimetres, the smallest divisions.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a unit of length?
solution: Kilogram is a unit of mass; metre, centimetre and kilometre are units of length.

stem: A car moving on a straight highway shows __________ motion, while its spinning tyre shows __________ motion.
solution: The car body moves in a straight line (rectilinear) while each tyre spins (rotational).

stem: The reason a passenger feels the trees 'moving backward' from a moving train is that motion is __________.
options: relative to the chosen reference frame
solution: Motion is relative; from the moving train's frame, stationary trees appear to move backward.

stem: To measure length correctly, the object should be measured __________.
options: with the scale's markings touching the object along its length
solution: The scale must lie in contact and parallel to the object's length for an accurate reading.

stem: Which of these is the largest length?
solution: 1 km = 1000 m, far larger than 1 m, 1 cm or 1 mm.

stem: Arrange in increasing order of size: metre, millimetre, kilometre, centimetre.
A blinking light that switches on and off at equal time intervals shows a change that is __________.
solution: Regular repetition at equal time intervals is periodic behaviour.

stem: The tip of a rotating fan blade traces a __________.
solution: The blade tip moves in a circle around the fan's axis — a circular path.

stem: Which activity best measures the length of a cricket pitch?
options: Using a long measuring tape in metres
solution: A long measuring tape in metres is suitable for the ~20 m cricket pitch.

stem: A quantity that has a definite standard, a number and a unit is a __________.
solution: A measured physical quantity is expressed as a number together with a standard unit.

stem: Which of the following shows both translatory and rotational motion together?
options: A spinning top staying in one spot
solution: A rolling football moves forward (translatory) while spinning (rotational) at the same time.

stem: If a measurement is repeated carefully several times, taking the average helps to __________.
options: reduce random errors and get a more reliable value
solution: Averaging repeated readings reduces random errors and gives a more reliable measurement.

stem: The main idea of measuring motion is to describe __________.
options: how the position of an object changes with time
solution: Describing motion means tracking how an object's position changes over time.

stem: Ancient units like 'angul' and 'mutthi' in India were based on __________.
solution: Traditional Indian units such as angul (finger-width) and mutthi (fist) were based on body parts, hence variable.

stem: Which of the following is the correct conversion?
The smallest division on an ordinary metre scale used in schools is usually __________.
solution: A school metre scale is graduated down to millimetres, its smallest division.

stem: 5 kilometres 250 metres expressed fully in metres is __________.
solution: 5 km = 5000 m; plus 250 m gives 5250 m.

stem: The spinning of the Earth on its axis is an example of __________ motion.
solution: The Earth spinning on its own axis is rotational (spinning) motion.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Measurement of Length and Motion' is that:
options: quantities are measured using agreed standard units, and motion is described as change of position with time
body parts are the best units
solution: The chapter teaches measuring length with standard units and describing different types of motion as changes of position with time.

stem: The process of comparing an unknown quantity with a known standard is called __________.
solution: Measurement is the comparison of an unknown quantity with a known standard unit.

stem: One metre is equal to __________ centimetres.
solution: 1 metre = 100 centimetres.

stem: One kilometre is equal to __________ metres.
solution: 1 kilometre = 1000 metres.

stem: To measure the length of a curved line, one can use a __________.
solution: A thread laid along the curve and then measured with a scale gives the curved length.

stem: The correct way to take a reading on a scale is to keep the eye __________ the point.
solution: The eye should be directly above the reading point to avoid parallax error.

stem: The error caused by looking at a scale from the wrong angle is called __________ error.
solution: Parallax error occurs when the scale is read from the wrong angle.

stem: A change in the position of an object with time is called __________.
solution: Motion is a change in an object's position with time.

stem: An object that does not change its position with time is said to be at __________.
solution: An object at rest does not change its position with time.

stem: The motion of a ball rolling on the ground in a straight line is __________ motion.
solution: Motion along a straight line is called rectilinear motion.

stem: The motion of the hands of a clock is an example of __________ motion.
solution: The hands of a clock move in a circle — circular motion.

stem: The motion of a swing or a pendulum that repeats after regular intervals is __________ motion.
solution: A swing shows periodic (oscillatory) motion, repeating at regular intervals.

stem: The motion of a spinning top about its axis is __________ motion.
solution: A spinning top rotates about its axis — rotational motion.

stem: Ancient people measured length using body parts such as the __________.
solution: Body parts like the cubit, foot and handspan were once used to measure length.

stem: Body parts are not reliable for measuring length because they __________.
solution: Body-part measures vary between people, so standard units are needed.

stem: Which of the following would you use to measure the length of a pencil?
solution: A short scale is suitable for measuring a small object like a pencil.

stem: The distance between two cities is best measured in __________.
solution: Large distances between cities are measured in kilometres.

stem: The thickness of a coin is best measured in __________.
solution: Very small lengths like the thickness of a coin are measured in millimetres.

stem: While measuring with a broken-ended ruler, one should start from a __________ mark.
solution: If the ruler's end is broken, start from a clear mark and subtract to get the length.

stem: The motion of the Earth around the Sun is an example of __________ motion.
solution: The Earth revolves around the Sun in a periodic, roughly circular path.

stem: The motion of a sewing machine needle is __________ motion.
solution: A sewing machine needle moves up and down repeatedly — periodic motion.

stem: One centimetre is equal to __________ millimetres.
solution: 1 centimetre = 10 millimetres.

stem: A moving car's wheel shows both rotational motion and __________ motion together.
solution: A moving wheel rotates about its axis while the car moves in a straight line.

stem: Standard units of measurement are important because they are __________ everywhere.
solution: Standard units are uniform everywhere, so measurements can be compared reliably.

stem: To measure length accurately, the scale must be placed __________ the object.
solution: The scale should lie along and touching the object for an accurate reading.

stem: The vibratory motion of the strings of a guitar is a type of __________ motion.
solution: Vibrating guitar strings show periodic (vibratory) motion.

stem: A ball thrown straight up and coming down shows __________ motion.
solution: The ball moves along a straight vertical line — rectilinear motion.

stem: The most suitable instrument to measure the length of a playground is a __________.
solution: A long measuring tape is suitable for large distances like a playground.
